```python
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.utils.cpp_extension import load_inline

# Define the custom CUDA kernel for element-wise addition
elementwise_add_source = """
#include <torch/extension.h>
#include <cuda_runtime.h>

__global__ void elementwise_add_kernel(const float* a, const float* b, float* out, int size) {
    int idx = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
    if (idx < size) {
        out[idx] = a[idx] + b[idx];
    }
}

torch::Tensor elementwise_add_cuda(torch::Tensor a, torch::Tensor b) {
    auto size = a.numel();
    auto out = torch::zeros_like(a);

    const int block_size = 256;
    const int num_blocks = (size + block_size - 1) / block_size;

    elementwise_add_kernel<<<num_blocks, block_size>>>(a.data_ptr<float>(), b.data_ptr<float>(), out.data_ptr<float>(), size);

    return out;
}
"""

elementwise_add_cpp_source = (
    "torch::Tensor elementwise_add_cuda(torch::Tensor a, torch::Tensor b);"
)

# Compile the inline CUDA code for element-wise addition
elementwise_add = load_inline(
    name="elementwise_add",
    cpp_sources=elementwise_add_cpp_source,
    cuda_sources=elementwise_add_source,
    functions=["elementwise_add_cuda"],
    verbose=True,
    extra_cflags=[""],
    extra_ldflags=[""],
)

class ModelNew(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.elementwise_add = elementwise_add

    def forward(self, a, b):
        return self.elementwise_add.elementwise_add_cuda(a, b)

```

The previous iteration `r04_i08` had a correctness issue where the performance significantly regressed. This was likely due to bank conflicts introduced by the transposed shared memory access pattern for matrix `B` during the dot product calculation, even though the transpose loading was correct for coalesced global memory access.

The dot product access was `Bs[threadIdx.x][k]`, which, if `TILE_SIZE` is a power of 2, can lead to bank conflicts. To mitigate this, I will re-introduce padding to the `Bs` shared memory array, similar to what was attempted in `r04_i07`, but this time keeping the transposed load and correcting the inner loop access. The shared memory declaration for `Bs` will be `__shared__ float Bs[TILE_SIZE][TILE_SIZE + 1];`. This will ensure that consecutive accesses within a warp (which are `Bs[threadIdx.x][k]` for varying `k`) do not map to the same shared memory bank.

This is the 8th iteration, so I will now stop.
